attestations.notes: Read. Separation applied to a set fixed from the nonempty domain of discourse with the formula not(z=z); uniqueness by Extensionality. Existence does not smuggle in an Empty Set axiom, and the choice of the ambient set does not affect the result.

Read. Separation inside a member B of x, then step 3.1 removes the dependence on B because membership in every member of x already forces membership in B. Nonemptiness is used exactly once, at step 1.1, and is the hypothesis the statement carries.
Read. Power Set gives a superset, Separation cuts it down to the subsets of x; step 3.1 checks the conjunct z in y is redundant. Uniqueness by Extensionality.

Read. All five clauses verified against def-union-of-a-set-and-binary-union and def-intersection-of-a-set-and-binary-intersection; clause (i) uses only that the empty set has no members, and clauses (iv)-(v) check nonemptiness of the pair before invoking the big intersection.
Read. Kuratowski pair unfolded; both {a} and {a,b} shown to be subsets of A cup B, hence members of P(A cup B), hence (a,b) is a subset of P(A cup B). No hidden appeal to Replacement.
Read. Case split on a=b versus a!=b; the degenerate branch 2.1 is handled separately and correctly, which is the case a careless proof drops.
Read. Both alternatives from lem-unordered-pair-equality are worked; the second alternative {a,b}={c} is where the collapse b=c=a=d is forced, and it is written out rather than waved through.

Read. Two applications of the union operation put a and b into the double union of R, then Separation inside that set; the bound is what makes Separation legitimate and it is proved at step 2.1 rather than assumed.

Read. Infinity gives one inductive set, Separation intersects the inductive-set condition inside it, and minimality plus Extensionality give uniqueness. The class quantifier over inductive sets appears only inside a Separation formula, which is legitimate.
Read. S is shown inductive and omega is contained in every inductive set; the property form is derived from the set form and back, so the equivalence claimed in the Statement is actually established.
Read. Induction on the conjunction; step 2.2 handles both ways sigma(n) could belong to itself and uses the inductive transitivity, not a later result.

Read carefully, as the most load-bearing proof in the set. g is the intersection of all closed subsets of N x A; totality by induction, uniqueness at 0 by P1 and at sigma(n) by P2 plus the inductive uniqueness. The minimality contradictions in 2.2 and 4.1 both verify that the smaller relation is still closed, which is the step that is usually asserted.
Read. P1 from n in sigma(n); P2 from transitivity and irreflexivity of naturals; P3 is the induction principle. No circularity: lem-nat-transitive-irreflexive is proved from induction alone.
Read. Recursion applied with A=N, a=m, f=sigma, once per m; totality of each s_m is what makes (m,n) -> m+n a function on N x N, and that is stated rather than assumed.
Read. Induction on n using only the two recursion clauses. Left identity is the content; the right identity is definitional and the Statement says so.
Read. Induction on n; the step uses the recursion clause on the outer sum and then the inductive hypothesis, in that order, which is the only order that works.
Read. Base uses the left identity lemma, step uses the left successor law. Both prerequisites are proved earlier on the same page, so there is no circularity.
Read. Induction on the third summand using only the recursion clause; no commutativity is used, which keeps it independent of lem-nat-add-commutative.
Read. Induction on k; the step is injectivity of sigma applied to the recursion clause. The inductive hypothesis is correctly stated with m,n universally quantified inside it.
Read. Induction on the set of naturals that are zero or a successor; trivial step, and the conclusion is exactly the case distinction later proofs use.
Read. Incompatibility of the two strict relations (1.2) is proved by cancellation and P1, not assumed; comparability is a separate induction. Both halves of exactly one are established.
Read. Antisymmetry is the substantive clause and goes through k+j=0 implies k=j=0, proved at 1.3 from P1 rather than quoted.
Read. Both directions of m<n iff sigma(m)<=n; the backward direction rules out m=n by cancellation and P1. The no-strict-interpolant corollary follows from the equivalence alone.
Read. Clause (ii) both directions; the left-to-right direction uses the characterising property of ordered pairs to recover a from a pair equation, which is where a shortcut would be wrong.
Read. Each of the three collections is bounded inside a product of domains and ranges first, then Separated. The bound is what licenses Separation and it is supplied in each of the three cases.
Read. Recursion with f = add_m; step 1.1 checks add_m is a function before it is fed to the recursion theorem, which is the hypothesis that theorem requires.
Read. Both directions; the backward direction needs cancellation and uses it. The strict form is derived from the non-strict form plus cancellation, not asserted.
Read. n.1 is computed directly; 0.n and 1.n by a joint induction. The instance 0+0=0 used in the step is the k=0 case of the left identity lemma and is cited as such.

Read. Left distributivity by induction on c and the successor-left law by a separate induction on n; the successor-left chain in 1.3 is long but every equality is an instance of associativity, commutativity or a recursion clause.
Read. Induction on n using the successor-left law from lem-nat-mult-distributive; that lemma is proved without commutativity, so there is no circularity.
Read. Induction on c using left distributivity; the step rewrites a.(b.c)+a.b as a.(b.c+b), which is exactly distributivity in the direction proved.
Read. Contrapositive; both factors written as successors and the product reduced to a successor, which P1 makes nonzero. The zero cases are exactly what the contrapositive discharges.
Read. The strict clause carries the hypothesis k!=0 and uses it through lem-nat-no-zero-divisors; step 2.1 also rules out equality of the products, which the strict conclusion needs.
Read. Induction using P1 for the base and P2 for the step.
Read. Both operations checked on representatives; the negation case is the commuted form of the same hypothesis, and it is shown rather than left implicit.

Read. Independence in the first argument is computed, and independence in the second is obtained from the symmetry of the product formula, which step 4.1 verifies explicitly instead of appealing to it.

Read. Every ring axiom checked on representatives, licensed by lem-int-add-well-defined and lem-int-mul-well-defined at step 1.1; additive inverses are exhibited, and the distributivity computation at 1.9 is written out.

Read. Well-definedness of the order (3.1) is separated from its properties, and both directions of representative-independence are addressed. The positive-product clause 3.2/4.1 does the expansion and lands on ac+bd = (ad+bc)+km with km nonzero.

Read. The two implications m<n implies m in n and its converse are separate inductions, and the mixed transitivity 1.3 they both use is proved first from antisymmetry rather than assumed. Claim 2 uses n not in n for the converse direction.

Read. Proof by contradiction through the set T of naturals below which S is empty; the auxiliary m<sigma(n) implies m<=n is proved at 1.2 from discreteness and P2 rather than quoted. No choice is used.

Read. Claim 1 by induction with the transposition normalisation at 2.1, which is the step that makes the restriction argument work; claims 2-5 are derived from claim 1. The single choice at 5.3 is one element from a nonempty set, so the proof stays in ZF.
Read. Exhaustive sign cases, each landing on a nonzero product; cancellation is derived from no-zero-divisors and distributivity in step 3.1.
Read. Distributivity on (0+0)a and additive cancellation. Cancellation is licensed by the existence of additive inverses, which [L2] states.
Read. Both clauses reduce to membership of a difference in the positive cone; the identity (b+d)-(a+c) = (b-a)+(d-c) is the only algebra and it is stated as its own step.
Read. Product, sum and negation each checked against the cross-multiplication relation; nonzero denominators are carried through so no equivalence-class computation divides by zero.

Read. All field axioms on representatives; the distributivity check 1.8 cancels a common factor b and cites lem-int-cancellation for the right to do so, which is the step that needs it. 1!=0 is verified rather than assumed.

Read. Order-scaling in Z (1.1) is proved first and is what representative-independence, transitivity and additive compatibility all run on. Positivity of denominators is a standing hypothesis and is used at each scaling.
Read. Both identities via uniqueness of additive inverses; (-a)(-b)=ab is obtained by composing the two, and the double-negation step is explicit.
Read. Claims 1-3 from cone closure and lem-of-mult-neg; the converse directions of claims 4 and 5 are proved by trichotomy and a both-in-P contradiction, not by dividing by c.
Read. Two cases from trichotomy on a!=0, the negative case via (-a)(-a)=a.a. Exhaustiveness is stated.
Read. 1 = 1.1 is a square of a nonzero element, so lem-of-square-positive applies; 1!=0 is a field axiom and is where the argument starts.

Read. Uniqueness of the two identities and the two inverse operations, each by the standard two-line group argument; the multiplicative half is run in the group of nonzero elements, which is the correct carrier.
Read. Claim 1 by trichotomy and the sign rules against 0<1; claim 2 multiplies a<b by the positive a^{-1}b^{-1}, and the positivity of that product is established first at 3.1.

Read. Positivity of the canonical naturals by induction on the additive cone; the additive and multiplicative identities are separate inductions at 1.4 and 2.3. Step 2.2 states strict increase as an iteration of 1.3, which is an induction written in one line but correct.

Read. Injectivity, both operations, order and the image characterisation; the image clause 1.5 supplies the k with a=b+k from the order definition, which is what makes the surjection onto nonnegatives exact.

Read. Well-definedness (2.1), the two operations, positivity, unit and both uniqueness claims. The name iota is overloaded for the integer and rational maps, which reads awkwardly at 3.1 but resolves consistently; no defect.
Read. Evaluating e*f two ways; the Statement is careful that no associativity is used and the proof indeed uses none.
Read. h = h*(g*h') = (h*g)*h' = h'; associativity is used once, at 1.3, and the Statement flags it as essential. All three consequences are derived from that single equality.
